newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Armed Tajik group holds U.N. hostages.
newsitem.headline: Armed Tajik group holds U.N. hostages.

text.p: An unidentified armed group in Tajikistan took 11 people hostage on Friday, including foreign United Nations military observers, a diplomatic source in the Tajik capital Dushanbe told Reuters by telephone.

Russia's Itar-Tass news agency quoted sources close to the Tajik government as saying there were 15 hostages and that they were taken near Faizabad, around 60 km (40 miles) east of Dushanbe. The government and the Islamic opposition are holding peace talks in Moscow to try to end a four-year civil war.
The source said there were eight foreign nationals among the hostages, all working for the United Nations as military observers.
Another diplomatic source later said four Tajik opposition representatives had also been abducted in what appears to have been a hold-up of the observers' convoy, making 15 hostages in all.
U.N. military observers have already twice this month been subject to beatings and mock executions. The two earlier incidents were at the hands of Tajik government soldiers.
The U.N. mission fields 96 military observers in the republic and had its mandate renewed for four months last week.
